text.clef_octave_suspicious: The clef was read with a small 8 (an "octave" clef). If that 8 is not there, all {{notes}} notes of the part are an octave too low. What do you see on the clef?
text.note_out_of_range_high: {{count}} notes seem too high for this instrument ({{notes}}…). Were they read an octave too high?
text.note_out_of_range_low: {{count}} notes seem too low for this instrument ({{notes}}…). Were they read an octave too low?
text.time_signature_missed: From here on, {{measures}} bars do not match the time signature. Does the time signature change to {{time}}?
text.time_signature_missing: No time signature was read at the start of the part. The bars seem to be in {{time}}. Is that the time signature?
text.multirest_missed: This rest was read as a single bar. Is it a {{count}}-bar rest?
text.multirest_missed_no_count: This rest was read as a single bar. Is it a rest of several bars?
text.multirest_count_unknown: The number of bars of this rest could not be read. How many bars does it last?
text.measure_number_mismatch: According to the printed bar numbers ({{printed_before}}, then {{printed_after}}), some bars are missing. Is this rest a {{count}}-bar rest?
text.part_measures_missing: The other parts of the piece have {{difference}} more bar(s) here. Is this rest a {{count}}-bar rest?
text.part_measures_extra: This part has {{difference}} more bar(s) than the other parts of the piece. Does this rest last {{count}} bars?
text.part_time_signature_differs: Here, {{agreeing_parts}} of the {{parts}} parts of the piece are in {{time}}. What about this one?
text.clef_sign_suspicious_range: This clef was read as a {{read}}, but then the {{notes}} notes it governs fall outside the instrument's range. With a {{proposed}}, they would fit. Which clef do you see?
text.clef_sign_suspicious_change: This clef was read as a {{read}}, while the part was in {{proposed}} until here. Which clef do you see? (The answer renames the {{notes}} notes that follow it.)
text.time_signature_missed_section: Bars {{first}} to {{last}} do not match the time signature, but the next one does. Is this passage in {{time}}, before going back to {{back}}?
text.clef_sign_suspicious_missing: No clef was read at the start of the part: these bars are shown in treble clef. The rest of the part is in {{proposed}}. Is it also the clef at the start?

rules.title: Learned rules
rules.explanation: When you have answered similar questions the same way at least 3 times, on at least 2 scores, RECOmuse then gives that answer itself. Untick a rule to be asked the question again. "Undo my last answer" also undoes an answer given by a rule.
rules.none: No rules yet: they will come as you answer.

contexts.time_signature_missed: Bars that do not match the time signature
contexts.time_signature_missing: No time signature read at the start of the part
contexts.multirest_missed: Rest read as a single bar ({{count_read}})
contexts.part_measures_missing: Fewer bars than the other parts
contexts.part_measures_extra: More bars than the other parts
contexts.part_time_signature_differs: Time signature different from the other parts

note_position_mismatch.accept: take the note from its position

note_out_of_range.accept: move the notes by an octave

multirest_missed.accept: make it a rest of several bars

packs.title: Learning packs
packs.explanation: A pack shares what RECOmuse has learned with you: your answers to the questions (for the learned rules) and, if you wish, the corrections of your parts, which anyone opening the same scores will reuse. It contains no images and no scores. Send the file to the other members of the band: they will import it here.
packs.author: Your name (optional)
packs.includeScores: Include the corrections of my parts
packs.imported: Pack from {{author}} imported: its content is used from now on.

conductor.title: Conductor score
conductor.isConductor_other: This score is a conductor score with {{count}} instruments:
conductor.extractHelp: Extracting the parts creates one score per instrument, with the corrections already made on the conductor score. The conductor score does not change.
conductor.assembleHelp: Assembling a conductor score gathers the ticked parts (same piece) into one score, in the usual order: woodwinds, brass, rhythm section, percussion. Each instrument keeps its transposition on export.
conductor.alone: No other part of this piece has been read yet: open the other parts first.
conductor.noPages: Conductor score assembled from several files: it has no original pages. Open one of the parts to see its scan.
